plain: Sly and treacherous; secretly working to trap or harm.

webster.text: Properly, lying in wait; hence, watching an opportunity to insnare or entrap; deceitful; sly; treacherous; used of persons.

more.text: Intended to entrap; as insidious arts.

example.quote: With the same insidious views, they now seduced the members from the league, by representing to their pride the violation it committed on their sovereignty.
example.cite: The Federalist No. 18 (Madison, with Hamilton), Dec. 7, 1787
